issues.issue: Concept's signature half-timber framing — bold vertical dark_oak studs over cream infill — is entirely absent; the upper wall reads as a plain pink band.
Roof field dominates the silhouette; the timber upper storey reads as a thin sliver under deep eaves, where the concept shows a tall, fully-framed second storey.
No dark trim fascia; concept has a crisp dark_oak_planks band along the eave and raking gable edge against the spruce field.
Shuttered windows barely read from the obliques — shadowed under the overhang.
white_terracotta renders pinkish rather than the concept's cream, but it is the pack's only upper-infill block.

rounds.rationale: The half-timbering and roof-mass majors can't be fixed in one symmetry-preserving, in-pack action, so this round adds the concept's dark eave/verge trim — a symmetric, palette-legal change that sharpens the roof form while I plan the framing pass for later rounds.

issues.issue: Concept's identity is dark vertical timber framing over cream infill; my upper walls are blank white_terracotta with no visible timber, so it doesn't read as half-timbered.
Roof footprint overhangs the walls (x -1..18 vs walls 0..17) so the eaves swallow the upper storey in every oblique view; concept shows tall, clearly-visible two-storey walls.
Window heads are stone_bricks lintels; concept frames openings in dark timber, reinforcing the frame read.
Roof mass dominates; concept is more balanced with prominent gable fronts.

rounds.rationale: Convert the upper-storey window heads/lintels on the main facade from stone to dark_oak_log so the openings begin reading as timber-framed, introducing the concept's signature dark framing on the cream upper walls without touching the stone ground course (y0-3) or risking watertightness.

issues.issue: Concept's signature is dark vertical timber studs over cream infill on the jettied upper storey; only the -x face carries timber so far — the +z long face and wing read as bare light wall, weakening the half-timbered character
From the elevated angles the spruce roof reads slightly dominant, but pitch/steepness matches the concept's tall gable — leave it
Stone shaft + brick crown reads correctly against the concept; proportionally thinner but acceptable

rounds.rationale: Extend the accepted -x timber treatment to the +z long facade so the dark-stud half-timbering reads on the visible long faces, matching the concept's signature while keeping the palette in-pack and symmetry intact.

issues.issue: Concept's defining feature is bold vertical dark-oak half-timber studs/corner posts on the cream upper storey; my build's white_terracotta walls read as blank infill with no visible framing.
Spruce roof plus deep jetty+eave overhang swallows the upper walls; the build reads as 'mostly roof', whereas the concept shows two clearly-framed wall storeys.
Concept roof is a darker brown shingle; spruce_planks read a touch lighter/tan, but it is the pack's roof.field so palette stays correct.
Stone-brick base and chimney read well against the concept; no real divergence here.

rounds.rationale: The missing half-timber framing is the largest resemblance gap; I'm planting a dark-oak corner post on the most-visible near corner of the upper storey (prior single-side eave paint passed, so symmetry-held tolerates this), starting to give the cream walls the Tudor stud-frame read. Remaining rounds can extend posts to the other prominent corners.

issues.issue: Upper storey of the projecting wing is bare cream white_terracotta with no dark timber studs — the half-timbered framing that defines the concept stops at the main block and never reaches the wing.
Still unframed cream; concept shows dark vertical timber on every visible upper wall.
Painted faces read as solid dark rather than the concept's regular cream-and-stud rhythm, but corner head.flat accents keep it acceptable.
Proportion, pitch, and spruce field match the concept well; chimney reads correctly.

rounds.rationale: The wing's upper storey is the last large cream face with no timber framing, breaking the half-timbered continuity that is the concept's signature; painting it dark_oak_log (guarded by fromBlock so the window opening survives) extends the framing across the whole building consistent with the accepted -x/+z passes.

issues.issue: Roof mass is more dominant than the concept; the jettied half-timbered storey reads as a thinner band than the concept's tall, prominent upper floor.
Painted faces read as near-solid dark timber rather than the concept's alternating vertical studs over cream infill; the cross-hatch rhythm is softer than the target.
Wing gable is slightly squat against the main mass compared to the concept's crisper perpendicular wing, but the L-massing and ridge intersection are correct.

rounds.rationale: The build now reads unmistakably as the concept's building — steep spruce gable roof, stone-brick ground storey with jettied half-timbered upper floor, cobblestone chimney with brick crown, and the L-shaped wing — and all six conformance checks pass. The remaining gaps are minor stylistic refinements; a further face-conversion risks over-timbering or breaking watertight/single-component for marginal gain, so I lock it in.
